title: Ergotropy of multipartite entangled states in the quantum atmosphere
abstract: We investigate the ergotropy of tripartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) and W states in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole, focusing on how the extractable work is redistributed under Hawking-induced thermalization. We find that the two classes of multipartite entanglement exhibit qualitatively different ergotropy structures. For GHZ states, the ergotropies associated with different accessible subsystems organize into two degenerate families, whereas for W states they obey a linear averaging relation with no counterpart in the GHZ case. Under symmetric gravitational thermal corrections, the two GHZ families remain separated by a constant energy gap that is independent of the radial position. We further show that the Hartle-Hawking constant $D_{HH}$ and the normalized radial distance $r/r_h$ play competing roles in the evolution of extractable work: increasing $D_{HH}$ suppresses its recovery toward the asymptotic Hawking limit, while increasing $r/r_h$ enhances the ergotropy accessible to the observers. These results show that the redistribution of extractable work in a black-hole environment is governed not only by gravitationally induced thermalization but also by the structure of the underlying multipartite entanglement, providing a thermodynamic signature that distinguishes GHZ- and W-type quantum correlations in curved spacetime.
summary: This theoretical paper studies the extractable work, or ergotropy, of GHZ and W entangled states near a black hole horizon. It finds that the way work is redistributed depends fundamentally on the type of entanglement, showing distinct mathematical signatures for GHZ versus W correlations. The results highlight that local Hawking effects are governed by both the entanglement structure and the radial position relative to the black hole.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the extractable work (ergotropy) of multipartite entangled states is redistributed in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole due to Hawking-induced thermalization.
main_result: The ergotropy structures of GHZ and W states are qualitatively different, showing distinct mathematical relations (e.g., linear averaging for W states) and different dependencies on gravitational parameters.
method: The analysis uses quantum thermodynamics, calculating ergotropy based on the energy eigenbasis of the Hamiltonian applied to reduced density matrices derived from the entangled states.
model_or_system: The system models tripartite entangled states (GHZ and W) evolving in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole, utilizing the Hartle-Hawking vacuum.
key_observables: Ergotropy ($E(ho)$), which quantifies extractable work; radial profiles of ergotropy vs. $r/r_h$.
important_parameters: Hartle–Hawking constant ($D_{HH}$), normalized radial distance ($r/r_h$), and the entanglement structure (GHZ vs. W).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the context of the Hartle–Hawking vacuum, and specific Hamiltonian forms are used to isolate gravitational contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the nonmonotonic radial profiles of the four GHZ ergotropies and the ergotropy of W state subsystems as functions of $r/r_h$ under varying $D_{HH}$ values.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the Schwarzschild geometry and Dirac field quantization, then defines ergotropy, analyzing the GHZ state first, followed by detailed calculations and comparisons with the W state.
why_interesting: It connects fundamental concepts from quantum information (entanglement structure) with gravitational thermodynamics (Hawking radiation/curved spacetime), providing a novel thermodynamic signature for entanglement in extreme environments.
